chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan al-Attar, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He who treats his prayer lightly will not attain my intercession; he will not come to me at the Pool (al-Hawd). By Allah, he who drinks the intoxicant will not attain my intercession; he will not come to me at the Pool. By Allah.'

key_terms.الْحَوْضَ: The Pool (of the Prophet on Judgment Day)

ai.seo_question: Who will not attain the Prophet's intercession according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* emphasizes the foundational status of Salah and the prohibition of Khamr (intoxicants) as primary criteria for receiving the Prophet's intercession (Shafa'ah) and approaching him at the Pool (al-Hawd). In Shia scholarship, this links the ritual purity of the body from intoxicants with the spiritual integrity of the soul through consistent prayer, serving as a dual gatekeeper for the Day of Judgment.
